Article 6
Protection of women from violence includes protection of women in the household, in the community, in the workplace and in conflict and disaster areas.
Protection of women from violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes women with disabilities, elderly women.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region of Paser Regency.
Regent is the Regent of Paser Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
Physical violence is an act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
Household neglect is any person who neglects another person in their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence Protection is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and mental to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror and violence from any party given at the investigation, inquiry, determination and examination stages in court proceedings.
Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in fulfilling their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
Service is an action that must be immediately taken for the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim (woman) will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband-wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and their children, and mother and their children.
Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house Gender is a characteristic inherent to men and women that is socially and culturally constructed.
Gender injustice is a system and structure in which both men and women become victims of that system.
Gender justice is a condition where fair treatment is created for men and women by considering experiences, needs, difficulties, concerns as women and also as men Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and defense and security activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.
Gender mainstreaming (PUG) is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs.

Article 14
The Manpower Office and the Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises Office empower women victims of violence.
In empowering women as referred to in paragraph (1), implementation shall be carried out in accordance with the people's economic empowerment program.
The people's economic empowerment program as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted through: increasing the economic productivity of local women by providing entrepreneurship guidance for women in micro and small enterprises;
developing models for increasing women's economic productivity through partnerships between local government and the community.

CHAPTER XII
PROVISIONS ON SANCTIONS
Article 33
Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women thereby causing violence to occur, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
If officials appointed to provide protection do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
Service managers who carry out service duties in violation of service principles may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms of the applicable laws and regulations.

4.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 8 explicitly lists prevention measures including “melakukan pendidikan tentang nilai-nilai anti kekerasan terhadap perempuan” (conduct education on anti-violence values toward women). This is a clear, direct education-based primary prevention provision. The retrieved English candidate [4.4-10] accurately contains this same point, and the judge’s rationale correctly relied on it. Therefore the predicted “Yes” aligns with the source text, and the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

6.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions protection in the workplace and empowerment related to work and earning a living, it does not explicitly identify women workers/employees as a specific target group with special protection measures; targets are framed as “every woman” or women victims of violence.

6.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes the workplace as a setting covered by the regulation: Pasal 6(1) states protection includes “di tempat kerja” (in the workplace). It also explicitly mentions women victims of violence “di tempat kerja” in Pasal 13(1) (women victims of violence in the family/community including conflict areas and in the workplace have the right to be empowered). These provisions indicate the policy does address women in work/employment contexts (at least as a covered setting/affected group). The retrieved English candidates included this key evidence ([6.3-7] and [6.3-17]), so retrieval was not the problem. The judge nevertheless answered No because it required an explicit named subgroup “women workers/employees” with special measures; that is an overly strict reading given the policy’s explicit workplace coverage. Thus there is an evaluation failure, and the golden “Yes” label appears consistent with the Indonesian text.
